intent: What does a Pablo Creek Reserve homeowner have to clear before artificial turf, a putting green or a dog area goes into the yard, and how much of the lot can it cover?
distinctValue: Pablo Creek Reserve's constraint is its own Architectural Review Board manual, not a public code. The Standards and Procedures Manual (effective June 23, 2021; posted on the association's Enumerate Engage site as 'PCR ARB Manual 2022') requires ARB approval before permitting, construction or installation for driveways, walkways, patios and anything visible from the roadway or adjacent properties; requires approval for all hardscape changes anywhere on the lot and for moderate landscape changes (no fee, approval still required); lists putting greens under 'Other Structures'; sets planted-share minimums (Cottage: about one-third of the front yard and no less than 25% of the rear yard in shrubs and ground cover; Estate: about 25% of the front and no less than 20% of the rear), with a compliance table on the landscape plan; bans fences used as dog runs; limits perimeter fences to open-picket designs about 4 feet high; bars golf driving nets as permanent improvements; requires fully automatic underground irrigation covering landscape and turf, to the water's edge on lake and Nature Reserve lots, and bars irrigation from lakes; approves only deep (artesian) wells; ties grading to a Neighborhood Grading Plan approved by the City of Jacksonville; and puts plat-designated Conservation areas under SJRWMD and Army Corps permits that prohibit clearing, filling or removing vegetation. The manual never mentions artificial or synthetic turf, so the page tells the reader to ask the ARB, through Marsh Landing Management Company, whether turf is allowed, where, and under which review category, and how the sod-era irrigation requirement applies. Open-picket fencing makes the Fla. Stat. 720.3045 visibility protection unlikely to reach most back yards here, so the page says to get the ARB's answer in writing and links the Florida HOA guide rather than repeating it. The recorded 2020 leasing amendment shows the Declaration is recorded in both St. Johns County (OR Book 2312, page 1763) and Duval County (OR Book 12128, page 1099), and the amendment itself was recorded in both; the page says to confirm the parcel's county. CHECKED AND DELIBERATELY NOT USED: the manual's review fees and construction deposits (dollar figures; the page names the categories only); the construction working hours (written for new-home construction; the page does not assert they reach yard work); the shallow-well depth range (the manual omits the unit); the brief's 'San Pablo Road' location (not stated in any source opened). UNRESOLVED: the Declaration of Covenants and Restrictions PDF and the 2025 capital contributions amendment are scanned images without a text layer and were not read; a newer manual may exist behind the resident login, so the page tells the reader to ask for the current edition.

sources.label: Pablo Creek Reserve Architectural Review Board Standards and Procedures Manual, effective June 23, 2021 (posted as PCR ARB Manual 2022)
supports: Cover: "Pablo Creek Reserve Architectural Review Board Standards and Procedures Manual Effective June 23, 2021"

Section One A: "The standards, policies and guidelines outlined in this manual may be clarified, modified or deleted from time to time, if in the sole opinion of the HOA and ARB, such changes are in the best interest of the community. In the event of such changes, future editions of this manual will be published."

Section One C, Items to Be Reviewed: "The ARB shall review and approve all plans for construction in the community including but not limited to the following improvements: ... Driveways, walkways and patios; Other improvements visible from the roadway and/or adjacent properties"
Section One C: "All required approvals from the ARB must be obtained prior to permitting, commencing construction or installation of any improvements listed above."

Section Two A: "Once a submittal is deemed complete and scheduled for review, the ARB will approve or disapprove (with written comments) thirty (30) business days of the review at the regular ARB meeting."
Section Two B: "All required information must be submitted to Marsh Landing Management by 2:00 PM the Wednesday before the next scheduled ARB Meeting."

Section Two C, item 6: "Landscape plans with specifications 2 copies – 24” x 36” as well as electronic version if available. Plans should include a table identifying compliance with the guidelines: For example: Landscape Area: Front Yard area: 4692 SF; Min landscape area required @ 33% 1548 SF; Landscape area per plan 1562 SF; Rear /side yard area: 6454SF; Min landscape area required @ 25% 1614SF"
Section Two B, item 11: "Signed ARB Submittal Form with corresponding photos and samples"

Section Two E: "NO REVIEW FEE REQUIRED FOR: GENERAL REPAIR AND UPKEEP, RE-ROOFING, MAINTENANCE PAINTING, MODERATE LANDSCAPE CHANGES, WHEN UTILIZING SAME COLOR, SAME MATERIAL. ARB APPROVAL IS REQUIRED FOR ALL MAINTENANCE CHANGES."
Section Two E, item 9: "OTHER STRUCTURES (GAZEBOS, PERGOLA, PUTTING GREENS, WATER FEATURE, ETC.)"; item 10: "MAJOR LANDSCAPING MODIFICATIONS - after Construction Deposit is returned."

Section Two E: "Projects / requests not started within 120 days from date of the Approved Stamped Plans are voided and must be resubmitted with the review fee which may be refunded if no changes are required."

Section Two E: "ANY WORK THAT IS STARTED WITHOUT FIRST OBTAINING ARB APPROVAL WILL BE SUBJECT TO A DOUBLING OF THE PROCESSING FEE. ADDITIONALLY, THE PROPERTY OWNER MAY BE REFERRED TO THE VIOLATION HEARING COMMITTEE (VHC) FOR A POTENTIAL FINE FOR A VIOLATION AND MAY BE ASKED TO REMOVE/RESTORE TO ORIGINAL CONDITION IF NOT APPROVED."

Section Three A, Easements: "Drainage, utility, conservation and other types of easements may in some cases be located on portions of a home site. ... Permanent structures including patio decks and swimming pools cannot be constructed within these easements. ... The site plan submittal must reflect any easements located on the home site."

Section Three A, Existing Trees: "Where trees are to be preserved, care should be taken to prevent unnecessary disruption of the root systems. ... Trees between the curb and sidewalk will not be removed without ARB Approval."
Section Two B, item 1(c): "Location of all street scape trees, existing trees and palms over 6 inches in diameter, reflecting those trees to be removed and those to be preserved"

Recreational Equipment: "Play Structures may be permitted on Lake Home Sites on the side of the home only, not in the backyard." and "Other recreational equipment including croquet wickets, horseshoe pits, volleyball, tennis and badminton nets, golf driving nets, baseball nets, soccer nets, skateboard ramps, and plastic playhouses, baby plastic pools, and above ground pools are not permitted as permanent improvements on any home site, and must be moved out of view when not in use."

Section E, Fencing Standards: "Wherever fences are utilized, they should conform to an open-picket architectural design consisting of black or dark bronze wrought iron or high quality aluminum. Perimeter fencing should be a maximum of 4’- 0” high unless specifically approved by the ARB." and "Perimeter fencing adjacent to lakes should extend across the rear lot line (top of lake bank) and not to the water’s edge."

Dog Runs/Pet Fencing: "The use of fences to create a dog run is not permitted on any home site. Electronic underground fencing (invisible fencing) to control pets is encouraged as an alternative to perimeter fencing."

Section F, Landscape Guidelines, Overview: "Pablo Creek Reserve is located on a unique site comprised of sandy ridges, pine flatlands and pristine wetland preserves. ... the recommended design character for Pablo Creek Reserve should emphasize a natural appearance rather than formal, rigid plantings. ... All hardscape changes regardless of location on the property must be approved by ARB before work is to commence."
Section F: "Easement and street trees must not be removed or trimmed by owner without ARB approval."

Cottage Home Site, Front Yard: "Approximately 33% (one-third) of the overall front yard area should consist of shrubs and ground covers." and "Landscape material installed within screened enclosures will not be counted toward meeting these minimum landscape requirements." and "Front yard landscaping including irrigation should include the portion of the right-of-way between the front lot line and the back of the curb of the roadway."
Cottage Home sites, Side and Rear Yard: "Together with the foundation planting, no less than 25% (one- quarter) of the rear yard must consist of shrub and ground cover plantings."
Estate Home site, Front Yard: "Approximately 25% (one- quarter) of the front yard area should consist of shrubs and ground covers."
Estate Home sites, Side and Rear Yard: "Together with the foundation planting, no less than 20% (one-fifth) of the rear yard should consist of shrub and ground cover plantings."

Irrigation System: "All landscape material installed on each home site should be irrigated with a fully automatic underground irrigation system. Each system should be designed with adequate capacity to provide full coverage for the landscape and turf installed on the home site, to include banks if on a lake ... Where a home site touches the edge of a lake or Nature Reserve, the Owner is responsible for the installation and maintenance of landscape and irrigation to the edge of the water or Nature Reserve. ... sodded areas should utilize rotor heads. ... Irrigation systems are not permitted from lakes."

Well System: "The only type of well approved is a deep well, sometimes referred to as an Artesian Well. Shallow wells 70 to 150 deep are not considered Deep Wells by the ARB as the iron can cause rust on sidewalks and homes."

Hold Harmless Agreement: "We understand the compliance with all applicable building codes, governmental ordinances, the Pablo Creek Reserve PUD Ordinance and rules and regulations of the Pablo Creek Reserve Homeowners Association is the responsibility of the Owner/Contractor."

New Home Pre-Construction Agreement, Drainage: "It is the Builder’s sole responsibility to ensure the lot is graded in accordance with the community’s Neighborhood Grading Plan as approved by the City of Jacksonville."

New Home Pre-Construction Agreement, Conservation Areas: "Areas within the community designated as “Conservation” on the recorded plats are areas governed by the terms and conditions of the construction permit issued by St Johns River Water Management District and the Army Corps of Engineers. These permits prohibit the construction, clearing, filling, and cutting of trees or removal of any vegetation within these “Conservation” areas."

Pool Addition Pre-Construction Agreement: "Homeowners must maintain a list of all sub-contractors installing their pool on “Gate Access.net”. If sub contractors are not listed on Gate Access.Net they will not be allowed entry into PCR under any circumstances."

Searched the full text for "artificial", "synthetic" and "turf": the only use of "turf" is the irrigation clause's "landscape and turf installed on the home site"; artificial or synthetic turf is not mentioned.

sources.label: Fla. Stat. 720.3045: installation, display, and storage of items (2026 Florida Statutes)
supports: "720.3045 Installation, display, and storage of items. — Regardless of any covenants, restrictions, bylaws, rules, or requirements of an association, and unless prohibited by general law or local ordinance, an association may not restrict parcel owners or their tenants from installing, displaying, or storing any items on a parcel which are not visible from the parcel’s frontage or an adjacent parcel, an adjacent common area, or a community golf course, including, but not limited to, artificial turf, boats, flags, vegetable gardens, clotheslines, and recreational vehicles."
